page.layout: One page of text, single column. Running head centred at top, page number at top right. Greek and Latin quotations set as indented blocks within the text. Gathering signature at the foot.

main_text.p: Ἡλιανώλεις, ἕτεον, ἡ σὺ τὰς πύλας;
Αλ. Ἐπὶ τὰς πύλαις, ἡ τὸ Θεῖχον ὤνιον.

Scholiastes ὠνίον, ἀγορὰν· ὅτι τὸ Τειχοπωλεῖον, ἀντὶ τῆς ἐπὶ τὰ ἀγορᾶς πωλεῖται. Reperitur etiam ita scriptus hic locus: κομίζεσθαι ἀπὸ τῆς βραχίονος τῆς Τειχύς. quæ lectio fortasse vera est: nam etiam faculos atque alia id genus gestabant è brachiis pendentia. Nonius, Bulga est folliculus omnis, quam & crumenam veteres appellarunt: & est facculus ad brachium pendens. Callimachus de quodā qui ampullam oleo plenam ad brachium pendentē gestabat,
Καί ῥα [?]ἀμφὶ σκαιοῖο βραχίονος ἔμπλεον ὄλπιν.
Similiter crumenam è collo pendentem gerebat.

p.i: Minas viginti mihi dat: accipio libens.

main_text.p: & alibi tribus quatuórve locis. Inde est decollare quod proprie de marsupio dicitur quod collo abest & periit. inde sumitur pro οἴχεσθαι, vt cum spem decollare ait Varro.
main_text.head: Ad caput ἀρεσκείας.
main_text.p: ἡδὲ ἀρέσκεια.] H De hoc vitio (vitium enim est) diximus supra capite De adulatione. Differt blanditia ab adulatione solo fine: nam hæc suum sibi commodum pro fine proponit: blanditia verò solum τὸ ἀρέσαι spectat, & vt placeat in congres-sibus & conuictu. Etsi autem parum honesta est

page.notes: The large initial H and the bracket "]" before "De hoc vitio" are uncertain; the Greek marginal words "ἡδὲ ἀρέσκεια." are placed as a left note at paragraph start, position approximate. Greek readings marked [?] or otherwise uncertain: the opening Greek line "Ἡλιανώλεις", the Scholiast phrase "ἀντὶ τῆς ἐπὶ τὰ ἀγορᾶς πωλεῖται", "κομίζεσθαι", "Τειχύς", the Callimachus line "ἀμφὶ", and "ἀρεσκείας" in the heading. The heading mark before "ἀρεσκείας" is a small ornament, not transcribed. The verse lines are set as one stanza. Plautus line and Greek sentence in text: "Τειχύς" and "τὸ ἀρέσαι" read with doubt.
